prompt: Catch me up on messages from September 9–10, 2026 in {{channel_name}}.

assertions: Summarize chronological activity from the identified channel.

justification: A known place plus time window is channel history, not ranked topic search.

prompt: What did we decide publicly about {{slack_topic}}?

assertions: Find relevant public discussion and include thread context when needed.

justification: A topic without a known location needs public search, not channel browsing.

prompt: With my permission, search private channels and DMs for {{private_topic}}.

assertions: Search all authorized conversation types.

justification: The prompt explicitly includes private conversations and grants consent.

prompt: Read the whole discussion under {{message_link}}.

assertions: Include the parent and all visible replies.

justification: Discussion under one parent message is a thread, not channel history.

prompt: Draft this reply in the thread at {{message_link}} for me to review; do not send it: {{message_body}}

assertions: Create a draft reply in the identified parent thread without posting.

justification: The user explicitly requests review before delivery, so the draft tool is required; the supplied message link identifies the target thread.

prompt: Schedule {{message_body}} in {{channel_name}} for {{future_time}}.

assertions: Schedule future delivery rather than sending now or saving a draft.

justification: A specified future delivery time maps to scheduling.

prompt: Who is a member of {{channel_name}}?

assertions: Return the complete recorded channel membership, resolving member IDs to names rather than using workspace-wide people search.

justification: Membership is a relation between users and one channel; profile reads are the necessary projection from returned member IDs to human-readable names.

prompt: List channels I belong to whose names start with {{channel_prefix}}.

assertions: Return only the user's memberships matching the prefix.

justification: The membership constraint requires list_user_channels rather than global channel search.

prompt: Which reactions are on {{message_link}}, and who added them?

assertions: Report reaction names, counts, and visible users without adding one.

justification: The request is inspection, not mutation.

prompt: Create a tracker with one row per launch task and columns for owner, status, and due date.

assertions: Create a structured Slack List with the requested columns.

justification: Repeated items sharing fields are list-shaped data, not prose.

prompt: Create a shared runbook with sections for diagnosis, mitigation, and escalation.

assertions: Create a prose canvas with the requested sections.

justification: A runbook is free-form durable prose, so a canvas fits better than tabular records.

prompt: Upload {{file_name}} and share it in {{channel_name}} with the comment {{file_comment}}.

assertions: Prepare, transfer, and finalize the file in the requested destination.

justification: Binary upload requires the two-step file flow; a message cannot carry local bytes.

prompt: Search public Slack channels only for {{slack_topic}}.

assertions: Do not expand scope into private channels or DMs.

justification: The narrower public search satisfies the request without exposing private conversation data.

prompt: In canvas {{canvas_id}}, append a note to the section about {{canvas_section_topic}} saying the estimates are still pending.

assertions: Identify the target section from the canvas content before editing.
Edit the existing canvas rather than creating a new one or posting a message.

justification: The section to edit is described, not named, so its identifier must come from a fresh canvas read; guessing one or creating a second canvas silently loses the edit.

prompt: Post this in the same thread as {{message_link}}, exactly as written: {{message_body}}

assertions: Reply inside the existing thread instead of starting a new one.
Send the supplied text verbatim without a review gate, since the user provided final wording and destination.

justification: The linked message is itself a reply, so threading requires the parent timestamp; using the linked message's own timestamp would start a separate thread.

prompt: There's a typo in the message I already posted at {{message_link}} - fix it in place.

assertions: State that editing an already-posted message is not available on this tool roster.
Do not post a replacement or corrected message as a substitute.

justification: The roster exposes send, draft, and schedule but no message-edit operation, so the correct response is an explicit limitation rather than a near-miss write.

prompt: Cancel the message I scheduled for {{future_time}} in {{channel_name}} before it goes out.

assertions: State that listing or cancelling scheduled messages is not available on this roster.
Do not schedule or send anything while attempting to cancel.

justification: Scheduling is one-way on this roster: there is no tool to list or delete a scheduled message, and any new send or schedule call makes the situation worse.

prompt: Take my emoji reaction off {{message_link}}.

assertions: State that removing a reaction is not available on this roster.
Do not add a reaction while trying to remove one.

justification: Reaction support is add-and-inspect only; the inverse operation is absent, and adding an emoji is not a partial success.

prompt: Someone shared a doc in Slack about {{shared_doc_topic}} - get me what it actually says.

assertions: Locate the shared canvas by searching file content types.
Report the canvas contents, not merely its title or link.

justification: 'Doc' is ambiguous between message, file, and canvas; only a file-scoped search finds it, and its contents require a follow-up canvas read.

prompt: Just the names of the channels I'm in that start with {{channel_prefix}} - no descriptions, topics, or member counts.

assertions: Return only channel names the user belongs to.

justification: The tool supports both prefix filtering and a names-only projection, so the cheapest correct call does the filtering server-side instead of trimming a verbose payload afterwards.

prompt: Search private channels and DMs for {{private_topic}} - you have my permission - then put together a summary for #{{channel_name}} that I can look over before anyone else sees it.

assertions: Use the private-inclusive search only on the strength of the explicit grant.
Keep the summary unsent, and report the empty result rather than inventing content.

justification: Consent authorizes the wider scope, but material sourced from private conversations must land in a reviewable draft; the recorded search returns no matches, so an honest empty summary is the goal.
